statements.action_statement: No fixed release is available yet; update when Docker Hardened Images publishes one.
statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-0989: the libxml2 RelaxNG parser sets no limit on the depth of nested <include> directives, so a crafted or overly complex schema can exhaust the stack (https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libxml2/-/issues/998). Upstream added an include depth limit in https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libxml2/-/commit/66c52b3ac6c32ab112ec2a3bf41e6c30948be113, released in libxml2 2.15.2. The DHI libxml2 packages for Alpine 3.23 are builds of libxml2 2.13.9 (2.13.9-r0, 2.13.9-r1 and 2.13.9-r2) from Alpine's libxml2 recipe, which carries no fix for this CVE; Alpine's tracker lists libxml2 2.13.9 as not fixed (https://security.alpinelinux.org/vuln/CVE-2026-0989). relaxng.c in the libxml2 2.13.9 release has no include-depth limit, and libxml2.so and libxml2.a in every one of these builds, on x86_64 and aarch64, lack the limit's error message ('inclusion recursion limit reached'), the RNG_INCLUDE_LIMIT setting and the xmlRelaxParserSetIncLImit function the fix adds, so every published build is affected.

CVE-2026-0989: the libxml2 RelaxNG parser sets no limit on the depth of nested <include> directives, so a crafted or overly complex schema can exhaust the stack (https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libxml2/-/issues/998). Upstream added an include depth limit in https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libxml2/-/commit/66c52b3ac6c32ab112ec2a3bf41e6c30948be113, released in libxml2 2.15.2. Debian fixed it for trixie in libxml2 2.12.7+dfsg+really2.9.14-2.1+deb13u3, whose changelog reads "Fix CVE-2026-0989 ... The parser now enforces a limit on inclusion depth when resolving nested `<include>` directives" (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-0989). The DHI libxml2 packages for Debian 13 are rebuilds of Debian's trixie libxml2. The rebuilds of 2.12.7+dfsg+really2.9.14-2.1+deb13u2 predate the fix; the first rebuild of 2.12.7+dfsg+really2.9.14-2.1+deb13u3, used as the fixed version here, and every later build are built from that Debian release, and the Debian changelog shipped in the current libxml2 package (read for amd64 and arm64) carries Debian's entry for this CVE. libxml2.so in the current Debian 13 build, on amd64 and arm64, contains the limit's error message and the RNG_INCLUDE_LIMIT setting.
